ai.title: Unified programmatic agent execution and file explorer
ai.summary: Refactored `runProgrammaticStep` to handle generator state, tool execution, and turn-ending logic directly, replacing the deleted `run-tool.ts`. Introduced `file-explorer` agent template that spawns parallel `file_picker` agents for comprehensive codebase exploration. Updated `agent-list.ts` and `base.ts` to register the new agent and adjust spawnable lists. Replaced `json-schema-to-zod` with `zod-from-json-schema` in `package.json`.

eli5.text: The system now has a unified way to run its automated agents and a new built-in helper that explores your codebase by searching multiple locations at once. Previously, tool-running and turn-ending logic were split across separate files, which made the flow harder to follow and maintain; that split logic has been merged into a single programmatic step handler. A new "file explorer" agent template was added to the registered list of agents, and the old file-pick agent now also spawns the file explorer as one of its available sub-agents. If you use or rely on these agents, you will notice smoother, more consistent behavior when automated steps end, and the file explorer will automatically fan out parallel searches instead of one at a time. This is live today for anyone using the agent

entries.title: Support running string of generator code in quick-js sandbox

ai.title: Support string-based generator code in QuickJS sandbox
ai.summary: Agent templates now accept `handleStep` as a string of generator code, executed in a QuickJS WASM sandbox alongside native function support. `backend/src/util/quickjs-sandbox.ts` implements `SandboxManager` and `QuickJSSandbox`, initializing a WASM runtime with memory limits (20MB default) and stack size caps. `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts` routes string-based handlers to the sandbox, preserving native generator logic for function-based templates. The change requires `quickjs-emscripten-core` and `@jitl/quickjs-wasmfile-release-sync` dependencies, with sandbox cleanup triggered via `clearAgentGeneratorCache`.

eli5.text: The system can now run step-by-step agent instructions written as text (in addition to traditional code functions), executing them inside a safe, isolated environment that prevents crashes or runaway resource use. When an agent template provides its logic as a text string rather than a built-in function, the backend routes that string into a sandboxed JavaScript engine instead of calling it directly. This sandboxing limits memory and stack usage so one badly behaved agent can't take down the rest of the service. It's live today, and when this cache is cleared (triggered by the existing cleanup routine), any active sandboxes get torn down along with the cached generators.

ai.title: Add logging to git eval runner
ai.summary: Added console logging to `run-git-evals.ts` and `run-eval-set.ts` to track eval data loading, concurrency limits, and promise settlement results. Rejected promises in `Promise.allSettled` now log errors with specific eval names/SHAs and reasons, and failed evals are recorded in results with status 'error'. This improves visibility into silent failures during git evaluation runs.

eli5.text: When the system runs its automated test evaluations, it now prints out clear messages about what's happening at each step instead of staying silent. You would see it log when it starts loading test data, how many evaluations it's running, whether it's limiting how many run at once, and any individual evaluation that fails along with the specific reason why. If you look at the output, you would notice it explicitly names which evaluation failed and records it with an 'error' status instead of quietly dropping the failed result. This is live today and affects anyone running these automated git evaluation tests.

ai.title: Rename handleStep to handleSteps in agent templates
ai.summary: Refactors the `handleStep` property to `handleSteps` across agent templates and execution logic. Updates type definitions in `backend/src/templates/types.ts`, implementation in `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`, and sandbox injection in `backend/src/util/quickjs-sandbox.ts`. Ensures consistent naming for step generator handlers.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes instructions that run the agent templates got a consistent name across the system. The property that controls how each agent step handles its turn was renamed from a singular form to a plural form (handleStep to handleSteps) across the template definitions, the execution logic, and the sandbox that runs generator code. This is purely internal housekeeping to keep naming consistent, so there's nothing you'd notice as a user, and it doesn't change any behavior or availability. It's already live today as a maintenance change with no user-facing impact.

ai.title: Add /subagent command, --trace flag, and subagent streaming
ai.summary: Introduced /subagent slash command and --trace flag for CLI inspection and logging of subagent activity. Backend now streams subagent response chunks to the client via a new `subagent-response-chunk` WebSocket action, enabling real-time visibility into subagent execution. Trace logs are written to `.agents/traces/*.log` files when `--trace` is enabled. CI test commands updated to sort files before execution to ensure deterministic ordering.

eli5.text: When you run the CLI tool with the --trace flag or type /subagent, you can now watch the assistant's subagents working in real time. Instead of waiting until they finish, their responses stream to your screen as they generate them, and a log file is saved to your.agents/traces folder so you can review what happened later. The developer tests now run in a consistent order, so results are less likely to change between runs. This is available today.
